question: What compound is formed when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to a beaker containing a small amount of copper oxide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper (II) Chloride**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Copper oxide reacts with hydrochloric acid to form copper (II) chloride.
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂O.
 
• Copper (II) chloride is a compound where copper is in the +2 oxidation state.
 
• This reaction is a typical acid-base reaction where copper oxide acts as a base.
 
• The solution formed is usually blue-green due to the presence of copper (II) ions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Copper (I) Chloride**

 
 
• This is a compound where copper is in the +1 oxidation state.
 
• It has different properties compared to copper (II) chloride, such as color and solubility.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation States of Copper**
 
 
• Copper commonly exhibits +1 and +2 oxidation states in its compounds.
 
• The +2 oxidation state is more stable in aqueous solutions.
 
 
 
• **Acid-Base Reactions**
 
 
• These reactions involve the transfer of protons (H⁺ ions) from the acid to the base.
 
• Metal oxides reacting with acids typically form a salt and water.
